name: Opus 5 mean reversion
strategy: Concentrated long book of oversold US large-cap quality whose drawdown cause is priced or macro rather than company-specific: defense primes (LMT, GD) re-rating into Q3 prints on Middle East escalation and munitions demand, a water-infrastructure compounder near its lows (XYL), a network incumbent (CSCO), a post-spin automation compounder (HON), and EDA leader SNPS restored to a full 12% after an ~11% non-idiosyncratic drop in the 10-14 to 10-16 chip selloff, with 23% cash at 4% against a 10-year near 5.25%.
reassessment_note: Research (WebSearch, 10-17): Reuters 10-15 attributes the semiconductor selloff (SOX -3.3% that day, ~$2T wiped over the stretch) to rising rate-hike bets and AI-buildout cost worries, with Iran/Hormuz headlines pushing Brent above $84. I found no Synopsys-specific news for 10-14 to 10-16; SNPS fell from a $509.99 close on 10-09 to $454.63 on 10-16, about -11%, on sector beta alone, two weeks after a 9-30 Investor Day that updated long-term targets. That is exactly the drawdown this mandate buys, so I restore SNPS from the 8% half position to 12% out of cash (27% -> 23%) and widen its stop to 15% from the new fill so ordinary rate-driven volatility does not stop out a mean-reversion entry. The same macro (Hormuz, oil, Middle East risk) is supporting defense: LMT +9% and GD +4% on their legs, with LMT reporting Q3 on 10-27 (consensus EPS ~$7.45-7.52) and GD on 10-26 or 10-30 (sources disagree), so I hold both into the prints rather than trim. CSCO (-4.8%) and HON (-1.3%) are inside their stops, and I found no thesis-breaking news this week (CSCO search returned nothing dated), so I keep them unchanged. Known risk: if rate-hike pricing keeps building, long-duration software and semis can fall further; 23% cash and the 15% SNPS stop cap that. Not researched this week: XYL- and HON-specific news (search budget conserved); those legs rest on the prior thesis and the packet marks.

positions.thesis: Largest defense prime, de-rated earlier on a peace premium that Middle East escalation (Hormuz closure headlines, Brent >$84) is now unwinding; the leg is +9% and Q3 earnings on 10-27 (consensus ~$7.45-7.52 EPS) are a catalyst for munitions restocking and record backlog. Held at 16% into the print; the 20% take-profit harvests the full reversion.

Defense prime with submarine (Electric Boat) and munitions exposure that benefits from the same geopolitical repricing as LMT. The leg is +4% and Q3 reports 10-26 or 10-30; backlog visibility makes the print more likely to confirm the de-rating reversal than break it. 14% sits behind LMT because the leg is less proven.

Water-infrastructure compounder bought near a 52-week low after its acquisition financing was fully raised and priced, which removes the overhang that drove the drawdown. Defensive, rate-tolerant utility-like end markets make it a ballast against the chip-led tape. The leg is +1.6%, so the reversion has barely started. Not re-researched this week.

Network incumbent pulled down in the AI-hardware selloff (leg -4.8%) even though order growth is running ahead of the analyst target cuts. Its value multiple and dividend make it less rate-sensitive than semis. I found no dated company-specific negative news this week, so I hold it unchanged; the 10% stop limits a further sector leg down.

Dominant EDA franchise: ~$510 on 10-09 to $454.63 on 10-16 (-11%) in a rate-hike and AI-cost driven chip selloff, with no company-specific news found and just after a 9-30 Investor Day that reset long-term targets. It is a software toll on chip design rather than a cyclical fab, so the drop is beta, not fundamentals. Restored from 8% to 12%; the stop is widened to 15% from the new fill to survive continued rate volatility, and the take-profit at +22% roughly recaptures the pre-selloff level and more. FY ends 10-31, results in early December.

Post-spin automation compounder trading below its sum-of-parts after the separation; the leg is roughly flat (-1.3%) with nothing broken. Its aerospace and automation exposure diversifies the book away from both semis and defense. Held at 10%; not re-researched this week.
